public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 11

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/11](https://www.erdosproblems.com/11)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos11

/--
Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption that $n > 1$
is not divisible by 4.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ 4 ∣ n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and two powers of 2?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l m : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l + 2^m := by
  sorry

/--
Every odd $1 < n < 10^7$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound1 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 10^7) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Every odd $1 < n < 2^50$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound2 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 2^50) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Suppose that every odd $n > 1$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2. Then the set of
primes $p$ such that $2^p \not\equiv 2 \pmod{p^2}$ (the non-Wieferich primes) is infinite.
This is Theorem 1 in [GrSo98].
[GrSo98] Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$. The Ramanujan Journal (1998), 283-298.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan (H : type_of% erdos_11) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ 2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos11

findings.description:
The theorem asserts `∀ n : ℕ, Odd n → 1 < n → ∃ k l, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l`: every odd n > 1 is a squarefree number plus a power of 2. The cited source has asked a different question since its 2026-04-05 revision. It now asks whether every LARGE odd integer is such a sum, i.e. `∀ᶠ n in atTop, Odd n → …`, and it labels the problem "open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation".

The two statements are not equivalent. I proved in a scratch file that the Lean statement implies the source's. The converse fails. Computation only covers odd n < 2^50. Suppose one odd N ≥ 2^50 is not representable but every larger odd n is. Then the source's question has the answer 'yes' while `erdos_11` is false. In the other direction, a computer search that finds a counterexample would refute `erdos_11` without settling the source's problem. That is exactly what the site's 'cannot be resolved with a finite computation' label rules out.

The docstring "Is every odd $n > 1$ …" reflects the site's wording before 2026-04-05. As a secondary point, the source asks a yes/no question, and the repository's preferred form for that is `answer(sorry) ↔ …`. The site made the same edit to problem #10 on the same morning ("every integer" → "every large integer"). This repository has already applied it to 10.lean as a fix (local commit 4288d0de, 2026-09-21, "align problem 10 with 'every large integer'"). 11.lean was not updated. For #10 the two forms are equivalent, because the ∃k absorbs finitely many exceptions. For #11 they are not.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/11 (page footer: "last edited 05 April 2026"): "OPEN — This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation. Is every large odd integer $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?" The revision history at https://www.erdosproblems.com/history/11 shows the 2025-10-20 revision as "Is every odd $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?"; the words "large" and "integer" were added in the 2026-04-05 07:58 revision. The same page says: "Hercher [He24b] has verified this is true for all odd integers up to $2^{50}$".
findings.suggested_fix:
/-- Is every large odd integer $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, Odd n → ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l := by
  sorry

Keep the current statement as a variant, e.g. `erdos_11.variants.all_odd (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) : ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l`, described as Erdős's original all-n form. Also change `granville_soundararajan` to take `(H : type_of% erdos_11.variants.all_odd)`. Its hypothesis in [GrSo98] is the all-odd form, and `type_of% erdos_11` would otherwise become an `answer(sorry) ↔ …`. I compiled these replacement statements in a scratch file.

findings.description: This variant keeps the non-asymptotic quantifier: `∀ n, ¬ 4 ∣ n → 1 < n → ∃ k l, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l`. The source's variant is phrased relative to the main question ("Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption …"), and the main question now concerns only large n. Read that way, the variant asks whether every large n with 4 ∤ n is representable. The Lean statement is then strictly stronger: it can fail through a sporadic exception while the asymptotic version holds. Another defensible reading is that the sentence records Erdős's own all-n wording. So this is for a maintainer to decide when aligning `erdos_11` with the site. The all-n statement is not refutable at small n: my sieve finds no counterexample with n < 2·10^7, n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 4).
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/11: "Is every large odd integer $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2? … Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption that $n$ is not divisible by $4$."
findings.suggested_fix: Either `theorem erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ¬ 4 ∣ n → ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l`, or keep the current form and say in the docstring that it is the all-n strengthening.

findings.description: This variant also keeps the non-asymptotic quantifier: `∀ n, Odd n → 1 < n → ∃ k l m, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l + 2^m`. The source's remark "proving this with two powers of 2" refers back to the main question, which now concerns only large odd n. Read that way, the Lean statement is strictly stronger than what the source describes. The difference again comes only from possible sporadic exceptions: Hercher's result gives n = s + 2^k with k ≥ 1 for odd n < 2^50, and s + 2^(k-1) + 2^(k-1) then covers this variant below 2^50. The all-n reading is defensible, so this is for a maintainer to look at together with the `erdos_11` fix. Allowing l = m is a reasonable reading of "two powers of 2".
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/11: "Erdős thought that proving this with two powers of 2 is perhaps easy, and could prove that it is true (with a single power of two) for almost all $n$."
findings.suggested_fix: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, Odd n → ∃ k l m : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l + 2 ^ m`, or keep the current form labelled as the all-odd-n strengthening.

reformulations.difference: The source defines Wieferich primes by $2^{p-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$. The Lean set uses the other common form: `{p | p.Prime ∧ ¬ 2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]}`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For odd p, 2 is a unit mod p², so 2·2^{p−1} ≡ 2 holds exactly when 2^{p−1} ≡ 1 (mod p²). For p = 2 both conditions fail (4 ≢ 2 and 2 ≢ 1 mod 4), so 2 is in both sets. The two sets are therefore equal. The implication itself, (every odd n > 1 representable) → infinitely many such primes, is word for word statement 'A' in the zbMATH review of [GrSo98]. The review says Theorem 1 is a more precise version of A.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/11 (current text; fetched through https://r.jina.ai/ because direct access is blocked by Cloudflare)
https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/ErGr80 (also Er77c, Er80, Er85c, Er90, Er92c, Er97, Er97e, Er97f)
could_not_verify: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan: the docstring label "This is Theorem 1 in [GrSo98]". The paper is paywalled. The mathematics is confirmed by the zbMATH review, which states exactly the Lean implication and calls Theorem 1 'a more precise version' of it. I could not see Theorem 1's own wording. The site paraphrases the consequence as 'a positive proportion of primes are non-Wieferich'.

Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd / two_pow_two: I could not check Erdős's original wording ([Er77c], [ErGr80, p.28], [Er85c], …), because the Rényi scans have no text layer and the 1990s papers are not in that archive. This is the reason the 'large' vs 'all n' question for the two variants is filed as questionable.
review.notes:
Main point: erdosproblems.com/11 was reworded on 2026-04-05 from "Is every odd n …" to "Is every large odd integer n …", and it now labels the problem 'cannot be resolved with a finite computation'. The file still states the all-odd-n > 1 form, which is strictly stronger. The site made the same edit to #10 that morning, and the repository has already applied it to 10.lean (local commit 4288d0de, 2026-09-21). I used the checkout's local git history only for dates and diffs of 11.lean and 10.lean.

The other declarations are fine:
- finite_bound1: Odlyzko's check to 10^7, correctly stated.
- finite_bound2: correctly stated. Hercher's theorem ('odd 1<n<2^50 ⇒ n = s + 2^k, s squarefree, 1 ≤ k ≤ 13') is stronger and implies it.
- granville_soundararajan: matches zbMATH's statement of the implication. The set semantics are correct (proved equal to the source's non-Wieferich set). Small nit: 'follows from Theorem 1' would be more accurate than 'is Theorem 1'. If `erdos_11` is rewritten, this declaration must stop using `type_of% erdos_11`.

Categories match the source: the three conjectures are open, and the finite checks and the [GrSo98] implication are solved. There are no status issues.

Checks I ran:
- Lean: `Squarefree 0` is false, so n = 1 is correctly excluded.
- Perl sieve, validated by reproducing Hercher's table 11, 29, 533, 849, 434977, 10329791: no counterexample below 2·10^7 for odd n or for n ≡ 2 (mod 4). n ≡ 0 (mod 4) fails often (first failure is 100), which confirms 4 ∤ n is the natural condition.
- No statement in the file is provable or refutable in a few lines.

not_demonstrated.reason: The defect is a quantifier-strength mismatch (all odd n > 1 vs all sufficiently large odd n) on an open problem whose truth is unknown either way. Proving the statement would prove Erdős's conjecture. Disproving it needs an odd n > 1 that is not representable, and none exists below 2^50. The two versions can differ only on an unknown exception above 2^50, so no concrete input shows a disagreement.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was produced; I bailed out. The one misformalization I reported, Erdos11.erdos_11, states the classical all-odd-n>1 form where the source now asks about all large odd n. Both versions are open, and they can differ only if an unknown exception exists above 2^50. So there is no short proof, no short disproof, and no computable input on which they disagree. The only thing that compiles is the implication from the file's statement to the source's version, which shows the file's version is stronger but not that it is false or trivially true.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only reported misformalization is Erdos11.erdos_11. It states the all-odd-n>1 form of Erdős's conjecture (every odd n > 1 is a squarefree number plus a power of 2), while erdosproblems.com/11 now asks only about all sufficiently large odd n. Both forms are open, so neither the file's statement nor its negation has a short, honest Lean proof. Proving it would settle the conjecture. Refuting it needs an odd n > 1 that is not such a sum, and there is none below 2^50 (Hercher's computation; my sieve also found none below 2·10^7). The two forms differ only if an unknown exception exists above 2^50, so no computable input separates them. The only thing that compiles is the implication from the file's statement to the source's. That shows the file's version is stronger, not that it is false or trivially provable. The two variants I reported as questionable (not_four_dvd, two_pow_two) are in the same position. No trivial_proof.lean was created.

not_fixed.reason: I reported this only as questionable, so I left it alone. It is unclear whether this variant should be asymptotic like the main question or keep Erdős's all-n wording.
Also reported only as questionable, so I left it alone. As with not_four_dvd, it is unclear whether the source means all odd n > 1 or only large n.

submission.summary:
I rewrote `Erdos11.erdos_11` to state the question erdosproblems.com/11 has asked since its 2026-04-05 revision: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, Odd n → ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l`. Its docstring now reads "Is every large odd integer $n$ …?".

- The old statement (every odd n > 1) is kept, unchanged, as the new variant `erdos_11.variants.all_odd`. Its docstring says it is the classical and stronger form, since one exception would refute it.
- `granville_soundararajan` now takes `(H : type_of% erdos_11.variants.all_odd)`. This change was needed because `type_of% erdos_11` is now an `↔`. An `rfl` check on a copy of the file shows its type is exactly what it was before.
- I left the two variants I had flagged as questionable (`not_four_dvd`, `two_pow_two`) and all other declarations as they were.

Only this file changed under the checkout, and nothing else in the repository refers to its declarations. It compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
